system.summary: Army kana substitution tables of 1877 (隠語表 第一号-第二十二号): 22 shifts of one cipher sequence against the iroha; table number written as header (四号, 第六号)

prior_solution.where: The contemporary plaintext is written beside the cipher on each draft (JACAR images). The 1877 tables are in JACAR C09084568800; the 1876-77 table system is described by Satoshi Tomokiyo, Cryptiana, meijiarmy.htm. No reading of these three drafts found in print or online (JACAR, Cryptiana, this repository, web search JA, 13 Nov 2026).

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose the targets and set the rules (protocol frozen by SHA-256 before any key test); a Claude agent fetched the JACAR images, transcribed, identified the tables, ran the frozen check and wrote up. No human visual review yet.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agent run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: JACAR item pages and PDFs fetched; the JACAR 内容 field interleaves the cipher and the plaintext columns, which is why the record strings look partly in clear.
Headers 四号 / 第六号 and the cipher-plaintext pairs identified as tables 4, 1 and 6 of the 1877 Army tables (C09084568800); all 22 tables are shifts (8 - 2n mod 44) of one sequence.

Frozen protocol: each documentary table applied to the plaintext reproduces the transcribed cipher for 95/96 (doc 1), 45/47 (doc 2) and 132/138 (doc 3) signs; 200 controls (the 21 other tables + 179 random alphabets) reach at most 0.188, 0.255, 0.174. The pre-registered H1 (one key learned on doc 1, applied to doc 2) failed (0.021), as the drafts use different tables.
Contemporary kana plaintext segmented, put into kanji and translated; doc 2 sign テ/マ settled by the cipher (レ = マ in table 1).

outcome.method_basis: The clerk wrote the plaintext beside the cipher on each draft; we transcribe and read it, and check it against the 1877 tables found in the archive.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule, certain + probable words: doc 1 35/35, doc 2 20/20, doc 3 41/44; 96/99 = 97.0%.

texts.label: Army Ministry draft, 1879: Kagoshima dispatch, notes (catalogue 2572)
texts.summary: The Kagoshima garrison's dispatch is not a campaign, so no campaign allowance; departure date not fixed; spare ammunition better sent from here.

reading_review.note: contemporary plaintext, 35/35 words; checked against table no. 4 (95/96 signs)

texts.label: Army Ministry draft, 1879: no huts to be built for the troops sent to Ryukyu (catalogue 2573)
texts.summary: No need to build huts for the troops sent to Ryukyu; Captain Masumitsu informed as well.

reading_review.note: contemporary plaintext, 20/20 words (1 probable, the name 益満); checked against table no. 1 (45/47 signs)

texts.label: Army Ministry draft, 1879: half battalion of Kagoshima ordered to Ryukyu (not in the catalogue)
texts.summary: Half the Kagoshima garrison ordered to the Ryukyu domain; the other half to prepare under articles 2, 4-7 and report missing items.
